_comment: What an extracted Pose3D-Windows folder must contain. Read by
tools/check_bundle_layout.py (the build and release gates, hashing the
checkpoints) and by pose3d/integrity.py (the client's machine, at
startup, name and size only). JSON has no comments, so every rule's
reason lives in its `why` — which is also the text a failing build and a
`stage` says who can act on the rule:
bootloader  loaded by Windows before any Python runs, so no check
written in Python can report it; the build and Diagnose.cmd
are the only places it can be caught.
pre-qt      would kill the app, or a feature of it, after Python starts
— checked at startup, before QApplication exists.
later       informational; a bundle missing it still runs.

rules.why: the application itself; if this is missing the extraction did not finish
the console build that prints the self-test where the client can read it; the windowed exe can only write to pose3d-log.txt
the interpreter itself; the client's first delivery failed with exactly this file named in a Windows dialog, from their extracted copy rather than the build
the Visual C++ runtime is not part of Windows; without it python312.dll, Qt, onnxruntime and OpenCV all fail to load with 'the specified module could not be found'
the C++ exception-handling half of the Visual C++ runtime; missing it fails the same way, on a machine that has never installed a Visual C++ application
the C++ standard library half of the Visual C++ runtime; onnxruntime and OpenCV link against it directly

Qt's Windows platform plugin; without it the QApplication constructor aborts with 'could not load the Qt platform plugin windows' before this application runs a line, so no Qt dialog could ever report it
the JPEG reader Qt loads by plugin; without it every imported photo shows as an empty grey frame and nothing says why
the .ico reader; without it the window and taskbar fall back to Qt's default icon
Qt's native style plugin; the app pins Fusion, but a plugins/styles folder that arrived empty means the Qt plugin tree was only partly copied and the platform plugin is next
Qt's software OpenGL renderer; it is what --software-gl and the 'Restart with software 3D' button switch to on a machine whose driver cannot give Qt a context
the inference runtime; without it detection raises inside a worker thread on the first project the client imports, long after the app looked healthy
the rigged character that drives both the 3D view and the FBX/mp4 export; missing it, the app silently falls back to a stick figure
the baked rest pose and skin weights that go with character.blend; the same silent stick-figure fallback
the stylesheet; without it the window opens in a half-dark palette that reads as a broken install
Blender runs this file in a separate process, so PyInstaller cannot see it as an import; without it every export dies with 'no such file' at the end of a long job
the three pose checkpoints (person detector plus both pose models); a missing or truncated one makes detection either fail or reach the network on the client's machine
the export engine that ships beside the app; without it FBX, BVH and mp4 export all fail at the point the user asks for the deliverable
where projects and exports default to; the app creates it if it has to, but its absence means the folder was assembled by something other than the bundle script
how to run an unsigned build past SmartScreen; without it the first thing the client meets is a warning with no answer beside it

PyOpenGL's vc9 freeglut/gle builds import msvcr90.dll, a runtime this bundle does not ship and Windows does not provide; PyOpenGL would never open them (it hardcodes vc14), so they are unloadable weight that makes the DLL audit unresolvable
the same, for msvcr100.dll; only the vc14 pair can ever be loaded
Blender's translations, hundreds of MB the app never asks for; the purge that removes them ran with -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue and so could fail without failing the build
